newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE robusta coffee rebounds on NY, Brazil news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE robusta coffee rebounds on NY, Brazil news.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures rebounded from earlier lows towards the close on industry and trade short-covering triggered by New York's advance and crop news from Brazil and Costa Rica, traders said.
"The news took New York up and London followed on short-covering," said one trader.
A Brazilian official said the government is at present working with range of between 18.5 million and 19.5 million 60-kg bags for the 1997/98 coffee crop.
But he stressed it was not an official estimate. Earlier projections put the crop at between 17.8 million and 30 million bags.

Costa Rica said the 1996/97 coffee production could fall to 2.3 million bags from 2.6 million bags. But some traders were suprised by the market reaction to the news as the trade was earlier working with a figure of 2.1 million.
Benchmark March made a dramatic turnaround, rebounding from the day's low of $1,203 a tonne to end at day's high of $1,230, up $18.
"This is quite a good close, well above the previous life-low of $1,225," the trader said. The March contract hit the low of $1,225 on December 20.
The contract started the day $5 lower and then lost further grip to hit the life-low of $1,203, pounded by active selling by Far East shippers.

A move below the $1,200-mark would take the market to the pre-Brazilian frost levels. Coffee hovered at $1,191 on February 18, 1994. Two frosts in 1994, one in late June and one in early June, as well as drought, destroyed almost half Brazil's crop and sent London prices to near 10-year highs of $4,140 in August 1994.
Traders said a breach of $1,200 would see the next major support at $1,140.
The day's volume reached 6,106 lots, dominated by the March contract. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
